description: ABIT* (Advanced BIT*) runs the batches of BIT* with two techniques from graph search. *Inflation* weights the heuristic in the queues, `g + ε h_hat` for vertices and `g + c_hat + ε h_hat` for edges. The first search on a batch uses a very large `ε`, so it heads for the goal like a best-first search and finds some path quickly. Once a solution exists, a second, final search continues on the same batch from the first one's tree and queues with a much smaller `ε`. *Truncation* ends a search at the first edge whose estimate, scaled by a factor `τ`, cannot beat the current solution, and leaves the remaining improvement to denser batches. Both factors shrink toward one as the number of states grows, so ABIT* stays almost-surely asymptotically optimal like BIT*. It also rewires from every expansion of a vertex, not only from the first, and never checks an edge twice once it has failed.

papers.authors: Marlin P. Strub, Jonathan D. Gammell
papers.title: Advanced BIT* (ABIT*): Sampling-Based Planning with Advanced Graph-Search Techniques
papers.venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
